transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um, yeah. I came in because I keep having these really nagging thoughts that I’ve forgotten something important, even when I’m pretty sure I didn’t. Like, I help with my aunt’s medicine sometimes, and I’ll get this thought afterward like, “Did I leave it out wrong?” or “Did I put something where it shouldn’t be?” And then with my classroom, I’ll worry that I didn’t set up the materials safely or that I left something where a student could get hurt.

It’s not like I don’t know, logically, that I probably handled it fine. I can usually remember doing it, or at least I think I can. But the doubt just keeps coming back, like it won’t let me settle. It’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should come talk to someone, because it’s starting to feel like my brain doesn’t trust me about things that should be simple.

When you have these doubts, do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking things over and over, washing your hands, or going through specific mental rituals to try to ease the anxiety?

Yeah… I do. I mean, I wouldn’t have called it a ritual at first, because it feels more like I’m just being responsible, but it definitely gets repetitive.

Before I leave the house, I’ll check the pill organizer if I’ve helped with my aunt’s medication, and sometimes I’ll look at the stove even if I didn’t really use it, just to make sure everything is off or put away. And at school, before I leave my classroom, I’ll go back over the same things—like making sure the lesson materials are where they’re supposed to be, nothing sharp or unsafe is out, that kind of thing.

Sometimes I’ll physically check it, and sometimes I’ll stand there and replay what I did in my head, like, “Okay, I put that away, I closed that, I moved that over there.” I’ll do it a few times until I feel calm enough to leave. It’s not hours or anything, but it does make me run late sometimes, because I’ll be halfway out the door and then feel like I have to go back and look one more time.
Do you feel that these checks or mental replays have to be done a certain number of times or in a specific way, otherwise you feel like you have to start over?

Not really a specific number, no. It’s more like… I’ll keep going back over the same few things until I get that feeling that it’s okay to move on. Like before I leave the house, if I’ve helped with my aunt’s pills, I’ll look at the pill organizer, and then maybe I’ll check the stove too, even if I know I didn’t use it. And then sometimes I’ll be at the door and think, “Wait, did I really check it carefully?” so I go back again.

At school it’s similar. I’ll look at my lesson plans or the materials, make sure things are put away, and then I’ll sort of replay it silently in my head—like, “I put that there, I closed that, I moved that.” I don’t think it has to be three times or five times exactly, but if it doesn’t feel settled, I’ll repeat it. Sometimes if I get interrupted or if I’m not paying close enough attention, it feels like the checking didn’t count, and then I’ll want to do it again.

It’s not a big dramatic thing, but it does make me late sometimes because I’m standing there trying to feel sure enough to leave.

Do you ever have thoughts that come into your mind that you don’t want or that feel foreign to you—like something you wouldn’t normally think about, but they pop in there anyway, and you have to push them away or counter them with something else?

Yeah, I think so. Not like… totally bizarre thoughts, exactly, but they feel unwanted. The main thing is this doubt that just pops into my head even after I’ve already done something.

Like with my aunt’s medicine, I’ll know I handled it, or I’ll have a memory of putting it where it belongs, but then this thought comes in like, “What if you left it out wrong?” or “What if you didn’t put it away the right way?” And it feels very intrusive, because I’m not trying to think about it. I’ll be doing something else and it just sort of comes back and grabs my attention.

Same thing with my classroom. I’ll leave after setting up materials and then suddenly think, “What if something wasn’t safe?” or “What if I left something where a kid could get hurt?” Even when I can tell myself, “No, you probably did it correctly,” the doubt keeps popping back in. It’s like my brain won’t let the thought close. I don’t want the thoughts, and they don’t feel useful after a certain point—they just make me question myself over and over.
When you have these intrusive thoughts, do you feel driven to perform these checks or mental replays specifically to prevent something bad from happening or to reduce your anxiety?

Yes… I think that’s exactly what it is, honestly. It’s not that I believe something definitely will happen, but the thought comes in with this feeling of, “If you don’t check, and something goes wrong, it’ll be your fault.” So then I feel like I have to do something with that feeling.

Like before I leave the house, especially if I’ve helped with my aunt’s pill organizer, I’ll go back and look at it again, even if I already know I checked it. And then sometimes I’ll check the stove too, almost like I’m trying to make sure there isn’t anything I missed before I can let myself leave. It’s not really because I calmly decided it was necessary—it’s more like I feel tense until I do it.

And at school, before I leave my classroom, I’ll do the same kind of thing with my lesson plans or materials. I’ll make sure things are put away, or I’ll stand there and mentally replay, “Okay, I moved that, I put that away, that’s where it belongs.” I’m trying to get the worry to quiet down, I guess. Once I’ve done it a few times, I usually feel calm enough to move on, but sometimes it takes longer than I want and then I’m rushing or running late.
Do you ever have thoughts about something bad happening—like harm coming to someone—that you can’t seem to get out of your head, even though you know they might not make sense or are unlikely?

Yeah… not like I’m picturing some horrible scene over and over, exactly. It’s more like this nagging fear that something bad could happen because I forgot something important or didn’t do it right, and then I can’t get that possibility out of my head.

Like with my aunt’s medicine, I’ll think, “What if I left it out wrong?” or “What if I didn’t put it back the way I was supposed to?” And I know, logically, I probably handled it. I can even remember doing it sometimes. But the doubt still keeps coming back, like it doesn’t accept the answer.

And with my classroom, it’s the same kind of thing. I’ll worry that maybe I didn’t set up the materials safely, or I left something where it could cause a problem. It’s not that I truly believe something is likely to happen every time, but the thought sticks in my head and feels important, like I can’t just ignore it. That’s kind of why I came in, because even when I tell myself it’s probably fine, my mind keeps circling back to it.

When you have these intrusive thoughts or doubts, do you feel like you have to do something specific—like checking, counting, or repeating something in your mind—to make the anxiety go away or prevent something bad from happening?

Yes. It’s mostly checking, and then sometimes sort of replaying it in my head. I don’t really count or have a number I need to get to, but before I leave the house or before I leave my classroom, I’ll go back over the same things more than once.

At home it’ll be like, I look at my aunt’s pill organizer again, even if I already looked at it, and then I might check the stove too. And I’ll tell myself, “Okay, you saw it, it’s fine,” but then I’ll get that uncomfortable feeling again like maybe I missed something, so I’ll go back and look one more time. Sometimes it’s not even that I expect to find anything—it’s more like I’m trying to get that anxious feeling to settle.

At school, it’s similar with my lesson plans or classroom materials. I’ll stand there and mentally go through what I did, like, “I put this away, I moved that, that’s where it belongs,” and I’ll keep doing it until I feel calm enough to actually leave. It’s frustrating because it can make me run late, and I know I’m repeating myself, but in the moment it feels hard to just walk away without doing it.
Do you ever feel like things have to be arranged a certain way or that something doesn’t feel quite right unless it’s done in a very specific or exact manner?

Um… I don’t think so, not in that exact way. I mean, I like my classroom to be organized, but that feels more like being a teacher and needing to know where things are, not like everything has to be perfectly lined up or arranged a certain way or I can’t function.

I don’t really get stuck on symmetry or things looking “just right,” if that’s what you mean. It’s more… I notice when something is out of place if it seems like it could matter, but I don’t think I have a specific way it has to be arranged every time. Like I’m not rearranging objects over and over until they feel perfect. At least, I haven’t noticed that.

I guess sometimes I do want things put back where they belong, but again, that feels practical to me. I don’t know if I’m explaining that well. It’s not so much about exactness or a certain order feeling magical or necessary. It’s more just… I prefer order, but I don’t think I have that “not right unless it’s exact” feeling you’re asking about.
Have you ever had thoughts that are violent, sexual, or disturbing in nature—like something you would never act on but still pop into your mind and upset you?

Not really violent or sexual, no. At least… not the way you’re describing it, like sudden disturbing images or urges. That’s not what I came in about.

For me it’s more these nagging “what if” thoughts that won’t let go. Like, what if I forgot something important, or what if I left my aunt’s medicine out wrong, or didn’t put it back the way I was supposed to? Or with my classroom, what if I didn’t set up the materials safely and something happened because of that? I know that’s not exactly the same as what you’re asking, but those thoughts feel really upsetting to me because they keep popping back into my head even when I know I probably handled it.

It’s like my mind keeps saying, “Are you sure? Are you really sure?” And I can remember doing the thing, but the doubt still comes back anyway. So no, not violent or sexual thoughts, but definitely disturbing in the sense that they make me feel responsible for something bad that could happen.
